## §3 — Mathematical Substrate

<a id="M25"></a>
<a id="s3-m25"></a>
### M25 — A distinction learns to return

The compact sixfold just constructed retains two terms and their four ordered relations. Its return must now become operable: a difference becomes definite, that determination can be repeated, and its result enters the conditions of another act. A triangle gives this inquiry a particular beginning. We can identify the figure, recognise its form in another instance and change the relation which makes its boundary an edge. The changes are distinguishable enough to be performed rather than only named.

Even the simplest judgment already performs more than its words display. To say that this figure is a triangle is to predicate a form of something held identifiable through the judgment. If the figure changes colour, we can still ask whether it is the same figure; if we draw another triangle, we can recognise the form without confusing the two instances. Identification holds an instance across differences, while predication makes a difference sayable. Both require a circumstance in which the comparison is possible. The statement, the instance and the field of comparison are thus distinguishable moments of one determining act. Putting them in separate boxes would still depend on the relating that lets the boxes be compared. This is the copula's work beneath the written “is.”[^s3-copula]

Before the terms have been assigned, QL writes their capacity for relation as `/ = −/−`. The two strokes on either side are not yet the values negative one and negative one. They mark places that can become determinate together. The first articulation, `0/1`, gives the relation its conscious circumstance: awareness and what appears. Here `0` names the unobjectifiable One; `1` names All, the manifest field in which an indefinite particular can be selected. The mark depends on its source for being and coherence. The source becomes articulated and knowable through the mark. These directions of dependence belong to one relation, but they do different work. A particular figure can disclose that relation without becoming the whole field or an image of awareness standing behind it.[^s3-native]

A figure becomes available for judgment before the judgment is settled. “What is this?” acknowledges that something has appeared sufficiently to be questioned; “this is a triangle” answers while remaining answerable to the figure. The next determination, `?/!`, holds questioning and asserting together. Without the assertion that there is something to ask about, the question loses its object. Without the possibility of being questioned, the assertion loses its accountability.

Determination also has force. Attention gathers around a feature and withdraws from others; a line is extended here rather than there. QL writes this differentiating movement as `−/+`. The signs acquire direction through their shared axis. Their distinction can be retained as polarity, or their magnitudes can be added and cancelled. The latter is a possible calculation; it becomes a mistaken account of the whole act when cancellation erases the axis through which the signs were opposed. The retained relation makes selection possible without declaring everything unselected unreal.

Selection becomes recognisable through recurrence. We identify another triangle because this instance can express a form that is not exhausted by its particular colour, size or position. In `X/x`, capital `X` is determining capacity and lower-case `x` its indefinite particular. The same letter keeps their relation visible; the difference of case prevents either from replacing the other. This capacity is not an inventory containing every already-drawn triangle. It is what lets a new instance be recognised and lets an apparent instance fail the test. Recurrence therefore carries both continuity and correction.

The judgment is also someone's judgment. `AM/IS` brings first-person presence into relation with third-person sayability through the second-person encounter: I am here, this is what I take the figure to be, and you can answer. The means of knowing belongs within this act alongside knower and known. Context includes the figure, our positions, the task, the available comparisons and what a mistaken judgment would do. In the original Gebser development, becoming contextual means caring for the outcome from within the situation. Adding more information to an aloof description would leave that participation concealed.[^s3-context]

The geometric construction gives this change a definite operation. Begin with a centre `O=(0,0)` and a radius to `N=(0,1)`. A second radius to `E=(1,0)` establishes an angle; the further stations `W=(−1,0)` and `S=(0,−1)` make the opposed directions available. The native acquisition order is **N, E, W, S**. The move from E to W crosses the diameter; it is not the next quarter-turn around the circumference. N, E and W bound a triangle. Adding S and joining the boundary in the order N–E–S–W–N produces a square. The former edge E–W becomes an interior diagonal, shared by the complementary triangles N–E–W and S–E–W. What previously bounded the figure now articulates its interior.

The triangle's interior angles sum to 180 degrees; the square's to 360 degrees. In these coordinates their areas are respectively one and two. Side count, angle sum, area and order of acquisition remain different descriptions of the construction. The gain is particularly clear in the changed office of E–W: the earlier relation survives, but its place in the whole changes. The centre, the cardinal stations and the circumference cannot consequently be treated as six interchangeable points. The centre orients the construction; the circumference carries its completed circuit; the four stations articulate positions within it.

The personed reading is a further, argued operation. First-, second- and third-person perspectives can be taken in sequence. Context makes all three available in one recognising act without installing a fourth spectator outside them. At `#4`, their claims to exclusive validity are voided; at `#5`, their belonging to one act is recognised; at `#0`, that achieved unity returns to `0/1`, the ground–appearance relation it never escaped. Three perspectives are answered by three operations of recognition: `3:3`. The latter three constitute one recognition: `3:1`. The geometric change makes the recontextualisation visible; its angle sum does not prove this account of the Subject. The derivation begins in personed experience, before its later physical, mental and musical refractions.

Exactness can now enter the context without claiming to contain it. In `∞/dx`, the indefinite horizon meets a local differential. Calculus provides a precise instance of what locality retains and what it cannot recover by itself. The functions `F(x)=x²+C`, for every constant `C`, have the same derivative `F′(x)=2x`. Integrating `2x` therefore returns a family. A condition such as `F(0)=3` selects one member. The derivative was exact throughout; what it lacked was the information needed to select the additive constant. QL reads this dependence as a demand that local determination remain related to its provenance, rather than as a defect to be cured by less precise calculation.[^s3-calculus]

The final turn, `1/0`, directs the achieved determination toward its condition. Ordinary arithmetic cannot divide one by zero. The native notation keeps this limit visible: the ground is not another measurable object against which the finished mark could be proportioned. Recognition changes the mark's relation to what makes it possible. It can preserve the achieved judgment, correct it or release the inquiry; none of these acts manufactures awareness as its result.

The traversal can now be compressed:

$$
\text{−/−}\;\longrightarrow\;0/1\;\longrightarrow\;?/!\;\longrightarrow\;\text{−/+}\;\longrightarrow\;X/x\;\longrightarrow\;AM/IS\;\longrightarrow\;\infty/dx\;\longrightarrow\;1/0.
$$

These are eight determinations of one passage: the parent relation and return bracket six qualitative determinations. Their traversal does not enlarge the six-position body into eight positions. The typed construction `B ⊔ (B×B)`, already counted as `2+2²=6`, retains the two singles and four ordered pairs. Following the judgment has now given those retained offices a qualitative articulation. The body can be counted, and the act through which it is recognised remains within its account.

<a id="M26"></a>
<a id="s3-m26"></a>
### M26 — The sixfold reads itself

Once the body can hold a distinction together with its self-relations, it can read its own parts from more than one orientation. This is stronger than turning a printed sequence around. We must distinguish a position in the body from the content that comes to occupy it.

Begin with the four explicate positions, whose outer binary contents are `(0/0, 0/1, 1/0, 1/1)`, held between the singles `0` and `1`. The pure contents, `0/0` and `1/1`, occupy positions 1 and 4; the mixed contents, `0/1` and `1/0`, occupy positions 2 and 3. The processual source distinguishes the corresponding Structure and Formality pairings, with the two implicate poles retaining the Essence axis. Now read the parent relation through its internal expansion. For `(a/b)/(c/d)`, relate the first numerator entry to each denominator entry, then do the same for the second: `(a/c, a/d, b/c, b/d)`. Retain the two singles beside these four relations. Each parent thereby carries a complete body:

$$
\begin{aligned}
P&=(0/1)/(1/0)
  &&\rightsquigarrow (0/1,\;0/0,\;1/1,\;1/0)\quad+[0,1],\\
P'&=(1/0)/(0/1)
  &&\rightsquigarrow (1/0,\;1/1,\;0/0,\;0/1)\quad+[1,0].
\end{aligned}
$$

The square brackets retain the singles as a different sort from the four paired contents. The expansion arrows state the native reading rule; these expressions are not arithmetic fractions awaiting cancellation.[^s3-parents]

Compare the positions with what each now holds. In the outer body, positions 1 and 4 carried pure contents; in the expanded parent they carry mixed contents. Positions 2 and 3, formerly mixed, now carry pure contents. Structure and Formality exchange office across that position-to-content reading. The Essence relation remains the axis through which the body is held. Changing from P to P′ then reverses the orientations of the complete expansion, including its singles. A reversal by itself would preserve the distinction between the pure pair and the mixed pair; it would not explain their exchange of office. The substantive result requires the nested comparison as well as the phase reversal.

Two other readings cross this body. Its adjacent harmonics pair `(0,1)`, `(2,3)` and `(4,5)`: Being, Becoming, and Knowing/unKnowing. Its complementary folds pair `(0,5)`, `(1,4)` and `(2,3)`: Essence, Constitution and Text-Texture in the qualitative account. The shared middle pair does not make the partitions identical. The harmonic reading follows the passage from availability through movement to recognition; the complementary reading brings the beginning into relation with return, definition with context, and force with pattern. A locally used name such as Structure must therefore retain the pairing and register that gives it its work.

The First Spanda gives this self-relation a process. Its starting `0=(0/0)` names the unselected relational capacity in native syntax. Emanation reads the ground through its first distinction; reversion reads the distinction through the ground. Keeping the actual nesting gives

$$
T_0:\quad \frac{0}{(0/1)}\rightsquigarrow\frac01,
\qquad
T_1:\quad \frac{(1/0)}{0}\rightsquigarrow\frac10.
$$

The two tracks make explicit what the parent `(0/1)/(1/0)` holds together. Their bridge is

$$
\left(\frac10+\frac01\right)_{\mathrm{QL}}\rightsquigarrow\frac11=1=100\%.
$$

The plus is the native composition mark. The later harmonisation writes `∨` to distinguish this from fraction addition; its Boolean companion below supplies one exact carrier, not a replacement for the native tracks. Evaluating its terms as ordinary real-number fractions would destroy the expression before its work began. The achieved One is the relation recognised as whole; it is not simply the positive pole with the other pole deleted. Emanation and reversion are correlative readings. Their exposition in sequence does not require one process to finish before the other exists.[^s3-spanda]

A small categorical construction makes the retained difference explicit. Take two objects, A and B, an arrow `f:A→B` and its inverse `g:B→A`. Their composites satisfy `g∘f=id_A` and `f∘g=id_B`. There are two objects and four arrows: two identities and two crossings. Both objects belong to one connected structure, and the return recovers the identity appropriate to its starting object. The structure achieves unity without identifying A and B as the same object. This is a precise carrier for the relation's two poles and four articulations.

The later Boolean companion works differently. Let a binary state alternate according to `s(n+1)=1−s(n)`. Its two-step windows are `01` and `10`; their componentwise join is `01∨10=11`. Each coordinate has been affirmed across the complementary windows. Writing this result as the slash-form `1/1` makes a declared change of representation, from a bit word to the native proportional reading. As a binary integer, `11` is three, not one. Nor does the join retain which window came first. It displays completeness of the pair's coordinate coverage, while the ordered process must be retained elsewhere.

There is also a linear construction that preserves both unity and orientation. Represent the two windows by `b=(0,1)` and `p=(1,0)`. Their sum `u=(1,1)` is unchanged by swapping coordinates; their difference `d=(1,−1)` changes sign. Both are needed to recover the original pair:

$$
b=\frac{u-d}{2},\qquad p=\frac{u+d}{2}.
$$

The invariant alone cannot reconstruct what was distinguished. Invariant and changing difference together can. Under the swap, `u` remains fixed and `d` changes sign, so the exchange of the original windows is recoverable from their two channels. These constructions disclose the First Spanda's middle through different exact operations: invertible crossing, complementary coverage, and recovery from invariant plus phase. None requires ordinary division by zero. Each makes visible why the achieved whole need not erase its two readings. A completed act can consequently become a datum for another act: what was an achieved result takes the role of an inherited condition. The change from result to ground is a change of recursive office, not the numerical equation `1=0`. Here the sixfold begins to retain history rather than merely repeat a shape.

The Second Spanda asks the completed sixfold to account for itself. Let `F` be its six-position set. A binary assignment to every position is an element of `B^F`; there are `2⁶=64` such assignments. An ordered pair of positions is an element of `F×F`; there are `6²=36` such addresses. Retaining these as tagged collections yields

$$
|B^F\sqcup(F\times F)|=64+36=100.
$$

The state assignment and the relational address are different kinds of object. Calling the total 100 percent normalises it to one whole; it does not identify the number one with a cardinality of one hundred. The 64 and 36 can be expressed as percentage shares of that declared total.[^s3-accounting]

Comparing the two counts is another operation:

$$
\frac{64}{36}=\frac{16}{9}=\frac{2^4}{3^2}.
$$

The ratio displays four binary factors against two ternary factors. Dividing the sum by four would instead give 25. The passage from total count to proportion must therefore remain visible. The `3:3` partition also has exact effects: the six binary choices split into two triples, giving `8×8` assignments, while the six-by-six address array splits into four three-by-three blocks. The same sets support different factorisations without becoming different sets.

The comparison of `4:2` with `3:3` requires equal care. QL's harmonic cross-reading is componentwise:

$$
H\bigl((4,2),(3,3)\bigr):=(4/3,\;2/3).
$$

It yields the fourth `4/3` and the reciprocal of the fifth `2/3`; inverting the latter gives `3/2`. Ordinary division of the two scalar ratios would yield `(4/2)/(3/3)=2`. From the declared harmonic reading, the relations follow by ordinary arithmetic:

$$
(4/3)^2=16/9,\qquad
(4/3)(3/2)=2,\qquad
\frac{3/2}{4/3}=\frac{2}{16/9}=9/8.
$$

This is how the two orientations enter the musical proportions. Their earlier subject-level meanings remain their source; the ratios give that architecture another exact reading. A numerical result alone would not supply the first-person recognition that `3:3` and `3:1` articulate.

The Third Spanda adds a phase-sensitive accounting. A singled-out actualisation, the 64 assignments, and a two-phase copy of the 36 relational addresses give `1+64+72=137`. These are separately tagged offices: the actualisation is the achieved whole, not an extra binary configuration omitted from the 64. The extra phase tag is an explicit addition to the address space; reversing an already counted pair does not by itself double that space. Its companion compression, `2⁷+3²=137`, is arithmetically equal but partitions the total differently. The fuller derivation and the relation `36·(16/9)=64`, `64·(9/8)=72` remain together in the technical return. No identification with a physical constant follows from the integer count.[^s3-third]

A sixfold can grow in two further ways. A developed field and its conjugate may generate six new relations by pairing corresponding positions. Criterion and Distinction, for example, produce Criterion-through-Distinction: a criterion selects which differences count, while encountering a consequential difference can require the criterion to change. The generated relation does work that neither isolated term performs. The complete exemplar runs from Continuity-in-Indeterminacy through Criterion-through-Distinction, Delineation-through-Difference, Arbitration-in-Crisis and Con-text-through-Diaphaneity to Resolution-in-Reconciliation. This is the native `6/6′→6+6′`: six generated relations, not twelve concatenated labels.[^s3-growth]

Distributive recursion asks a different question. Each of the six positions may itself develop a complete local sixfold, giving `6→6×6`. Thirty-six addresses are available immediately, but the content at each address still has to earn its place. The first growth mode articulates the relation between conjugate wholes; the second develops the whole within each position. Their composition can make a richer field, while neither obliges every subject to have six parts.

The same distinction between naming and doing matters inside the native body. Truth, Mind, Word, Logos, Son and Image are paired with Play, Need, Sacrifice, Decision, Love and Work. A determination begins from available possibility, selects under a need, gives something up in becoming articulate, decides, binds and produces. Both faces carry the complete constellation; one phase does not monopolise Name while the other supplies Power. A form becomes usable when its reader can enact these relations in a judgment or performance. What has been generated must now be able to move.

<a id="M27"></a>
<a id="s3-m27"></a>
### M27 — The mark acquires a phase

A mark can be repeated without becoming a different kind of mark. In Spencer-Brown's calculus of indications, calling the marked state again leaves it marked; crossing a crossing returns to the unmarked state. Writing `M` for the mark and `U` for the unmarked, the elementary reductions can be represented as `MM→M` and `M(M)→U`. Juxtaposition and enclosure perform different operations. Their distinction matters when a form returns into the space it distinguishes: a static description may now demand that the form be what its operation negates.[^s3-mark]

A Boolean example exposes the difficulty. The equation `r=1−r` has no solution in `{0,1}`: choosing either value makes the right-hand side the other. Giving the operation a next step changes the problem. In `r(n+1)=1−r(n)`, an initial zero yields `0,1,0,1,…`; an initial one gives the shifted sequence. Each step is definite because the argument and result occupy different times. Delay has supplied a domain in which the operation can run. It has not found a previously hidden Boolean fixed point.

Varela takes another route in *A Calculus for Self-Reference*: an autonomous third state enlarges the arithmetic itself, with rules governing how its expressions reduce. This is not simply a third instant inserted between zero and one. A temporal alternation, a third value and a new algebra are different responses to the difficulty. Each must show what it retains from the earlier setting and what it adds.[^s3-varela]

Kauffman's iterants give alternation an explicit algebra of observation and shift. An ordered view `[a,b]` and its shifted view `[b,a]` belong to the same repeating process. A shift operator exchanges the entries; a diagonal operator can give them opposite signs. In a real two-dimensional representation, take

$$
D=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},
\qquad \eta=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.
$$

Both square to the identity, but their order matters: `Dη=−ηD`. Combining them in the order `J=ηD` gives

$$
J=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},
\qquad J^2=-I,\qquad J^4=I.
$$

On a vector `(x,y)`, J produces `(−y,x)`. Applying it again produces `(−x,−y)`; four applications restore the starting vector. Thus the quarter-turn represents multiplication by `i`, whereas the exchange η alone has period two. The orientation has been constructed through noncommuting operations, not inferred from alternation's visual resemblance to a circle. Kauffman's account also admits choices of representation; this construction does not need a uniqueness claim to do its work.[^s3-iterants]

The complex number `z=re^{iθ}`, with `r>0`, now separates two aspects of change. Multiplication by `e^{iφ}` changes its phase from θ to θ+φ while preserving its modulus r. Conjugation gives `re^{−iθ}`; inversion gives `r^{−1}e^{−iθ}`. They agree on the unit circle, but elsewhere inversion also changes the radius. The native inverse-phase relation can be compared with these operations only by retaining what each one changes. The word “inverse” alone does not make them identical.

An invariant can persist through movement without storing the movement. If a continuous nonzero path closes at its starting complex value, its final point does not reveal whether it went around the origin once, twice or not at all. Choose a continuous lift of its phase to the real line, and the difference between ending and starting phase records an integer multiple of `2π`. The winding number is then recoverable. It belongs to the path with its retained lift, rather than to an extra property secretly lodged in the final point. A system that claims to remember its return must keep the relevant history.[^s3-complex]

Bohm's conversation with Krishnamurti gives fidelity through change a different kind of working. Recalling a spinning wheel and a thread running straight, Bohm distinguishes thought's relation to what is from the mere possession of correct information. The conversation then makes room for error: a person can make a mistake and acknowledge it instead of persisting in it. The image's relevance lies in this active correction. The mathematical modulus makes invariance under a specified rotation exact; the thread makes answerability perceptible in the conduct of thought. Neither supplies the other's proof, and the speakers' later disagreement about a common energetic root remains a disagreement.[^s3-bohm]

A determination can return without being unchanged in every respect. Its identity may be preserved while its orientation changes; its local description may remain exact while additional history becomes necessary. The recogniser who corrects a judgment also preserves something through change, but does so by undergoing the inquiry rather than merely occupying a coordinate. The next formal question is whether the coordinate system itself can change while keeping the earlier achievement usable.

<a id="M28"></a>
<a id="s3-m28"></a>
### M28 — The horizon becomes a coordinate

A failed coordinate need not mean a failed object. On the real projective line, a point is represented by a nonzero pair `[x:y]`, with nonzero scalar multiples identified. Where `y≠0`, it has the ordinary coordinate `u=x/y`. That chart cannot give a finite u to `[1:0]`. A second chart, valid where `x≠0`, uses `v=y/x`; the same point then has the perfectly definite coordinate `v=0`. On the overlap the coordinates are related by `v=1/u`. The zero belongs to the new chart. It is not the multiplicative inverse of zero in the real-number field.[^s3-projective]

Projective completion makes this change visible in the plane. The affine parallel lines `y=0` and `y=1` become, in homogeneous coordinates, `Y=0` and `Y−Z=0`. Their common projective point is `[1:0:0]`. It records their shared direction in the enlarged space. The all-zero tuple is excluded because it would specify no projective point. The construction has altered what counts as a point and the space in which lines meet; it has not overturned the original affine statement that these lines have no finite intersection.

Complex projective completion gives a related construction with a different dimension. The complex plane plus its point at infinity is the Riemann sphere, `CP¹`: one complex dimension, two real dimensions. In its reciprocal chart, the former infinity is again zero. Maps can extend through this change of chart even though the extended plane is not a field in which zero has acquired a multiplicative inverse. The containing space makes an earlier limit addressable.

The bilinear, or Möbius, transformation gives the change a testable invariant. Let

$$
w(z)=\frac{az+b}{cz+d},\qquad ad-bc\ne0.
$$

On finite points away from its pole,

$$
w(u)-w(v)=\frac{(ad-bc)(u-v)}{(cu+d)(cv+d)}.
$$

Every transformed difference acquires a determinant factor and two denominator factors. Arrange four differences as a cross-ratio, here using the convention

$$
[z_1,z_2;z_3,z_4]
=\frac{(z_3-z_1)(z_4-z_2)}{(z_3-z_2)(z_4-z_1)}.
$$

The added factors cancel between numerator and denominator. Four distinct admissible points therefore keep their cross-ratio even though their individual coordinates change. The limiting formulation includes the pole and infinity on the extended plane. This is the exact relation that survives, not an assertion that everything about a figure remains unchanged.[^s3-bilinear]

For example, `(0,1,2,3)` has cross-ratio `4/3` in this convention. Under `w(z)=(2z+1)/(z+1)`, the four points become `(1,3/2,5/3,7/4)` and their cross-ratio is still `4/3`. The transformation changes intervals while preserving a relation among relations. Native QL can meet this construction because the parent ratio of ratios already asks how two complete orientations belong together. The cross-ratio supplies a specified geometric invariant; the native parent supplies the earlier recognitive question. Neither can be substituted for the other merely because both use nested proportions.

Quantum theory provides a further, bounded instance of why the containing space matters. A pure qubit can be written as `cos(θ/2)|0⟩+e^{iφ}sin(θ/2)|1⟩`, after discarding an overall phase. Its ray is a point of `CP¹`, represented on the Bloch sphere. The relative phase is retained; the physically redundant overall phase is quotiented out. Pure states lie on the sphere and mixed states occupy the ball. This construction concerns quantum states and their equivalence, not a proof that an agent has experience or that a symbol's two terms are a qubit.[^s3-qubit]

A usable atlas requires more than a collection of viewpoints. On the unit circle `x²+y²=1`, omit the north pole to define `u=x/(1−y)` and omit the south pole to define `v=x/(1+y)`. Both coordinates are valid away from the two poles. There

$$
uv=\frac{x^2}{1-y^2}=1,
\qquad v=\frac1u.
$$

At the point `(3/5,4/5)`, the coordinates are `u=3` and `v=1/3`. Their disagreement is a rule-governed translation, not a disagreement about which point is present. The point excluded by either chart remains available through the other.

A moving point tests whether the translation does real work. Suppose `du/dt=2` at this point. Differentiating the transition gives `dv/dt=−2/9`. The two speeds have different values and opposite signs because the charts orient and scale the motion differently. Recover the height through either inverse coordinate:

$$
y=\frac{u^2-1}{u^2+1}
  =\frac{1-v^2}{1+v^2}.
$$

Both descriptions give `dy/dt=6/25`. The transition thus lets differently written motions answer to one moving object. To call a set of charts an atlas, we need their domains and overlap maps, with the required regularity and consistent composition on shared domains. A compact circle, sphere or torus cannot be one global coordinate chart onto an open Euclidean domain: the image of a compact space would have to be compact, whereas a nonempty open Euclidean domain is not. A whole picture remains possible; its being a picture does not give it the office of a global chart. Agreement cannot be supplied by declaring all perspectives valid. Nor does chart compatibility choose a law of motion; we supplied the velocity separately.[^s3-atlas]

There is a logical counterpart to changing the containing setting, but it changes a different object. A four-valued semantics can distinguish truth-supported, falsity-supported, both-supported and neither-supported statements. Represent these by `{T}`, `{F}`, `{T,F}` and `∅`, with negation exchanging T and F and designated values containing T. Give p the value `{T,F}` and q the value `∅`: p and its negation are designated while q is not. Contradictory information need not entail every conclusion in this semantics. Its rules, rather than the mere existence of a fourth label, do the work. The neither-supported truth-value is still a value in the system, not the unobjectifiable condition through which anyone can use it. Priest's further “fifth-corner” proposal and the objections to it concern that additional crossing; they are not settled by counting to five.[^s3-logic]

These constructions preserve a demanding form of continuity. An earlier description can remain true within its domain while ceasing to define the entire field. The new setting must show where it includes that domain, how descriptions translate and what formerly unavailable operation becomes possible. The move from perspective to context has acquired this formal body. Its human consequence is equally exacting: acknowledging another situation means making the passage to it answerable, including where translation fails, rather than adding its name to a collection of views.

<a id="M29"></a>
<a id="s3-m29"></a>
### M29 — A return can retain its distance

The circle's overlapping charts preserve an object across descriptions. A quotient surface makes another kind of return exact: a path can arrive at the same surface-address without ending where its lifted journey began. Start with the plane and identify points displaced by whole units in either coordinate:

$$
(x,y)\sim(x+m,y+n),\qquad m,n\in\mathbb Z.
$$

The quotient `T²=R²/Z²` is a torus. One unit square presents the entire surface if opposite sides are identified. Crossing an edge continues from the corresponding opposite edge; the edge is a seam in the presentation, not a boundary of the resulting surface.[^s3-torus]

Consider the path `γ(t)=[2t,−t]`, for `0≤t≤1`, where brackets denote the equivalence class. It begins and ends at `[0,0]`. Its lift in the plane begins at `(0,0)` and ends at `(2,−1)`. The two integers record two turns in one direction and a reverse turn in the other. A continuous deformation that keeps the loop based cannot erase that pair. The fundamental group `π₁(T²)=Z×Z` records these independent winding classes. It retains a definite aspect of travel, although not its speed, every bend or the traveller's experience.

The relationship between the infinite cover and the compact quotient is exact. Every surface point has infinitely many lattice-related representatives in the plane. The covering plane is not a second surface hidden inside the torus, and the torus is not literally infinite in area. Nor is this universal cover the torus's separate two-sheeted covering of the Klein bottle. Those maps identify different things. Conflating their sheets would lose the very winding that makes the return useful.

The native `4+2` reading has a declared place here. Four sides present the square; two generators articulate the independent winding directions after gluing. Sides and generators do different jobs. They are not the six cells of a torus: the usual quotient cell structure has one vertex, two edges and one face, with Euler characteristic `1−2+1=0`. The native coordination brings presentation and circulation together without renaming their combined count as a topological invariant. The opening in the familiar embedded torus likewise makes the need to keep a place unfilled perceptible; no consciousness is proved by the genus of a surface.

A sphere supplies a real contrast, not an inferior kind of world. Every loop on a sphere can contract to a point, while the torus has noncontractible winding classes. Both surfaces can support circulation. The difference is what a loop may retain under deformation. In the native uroboric image, the mistake is consequently the presentation of a local closure as though nothing exceeded its account, not the mere use of a spherical figure. A faithful sphere and an unfaithful torus-diagram are both possible.

Even on one torus, the law of motion changes what return means. For the linear flow `[αt,βt]`, an exact return requires a positive time T for which both `Tα` and `Tβ` are integers. Two nonzero rates with irrational ratio cannot meet that requirement. A bounded space need not produce a periodic trajectory. Compactness, periodicity and the possibility of winding are distinct properties; the dynamics decide which available paths are realised.

Music gives the retained interval an audible rather than topological operation. In just ratios, a fourth multiplies frequency by `4/3` and a fifth by `3/2`. Their composition reaches the octave because `(4/3)(3/2)=2`. Two fourths reach `16/9`, leaving the exact multiplicative complement `9/8`:

$$
\frac43\;\frac98\;\frac43=2,
\qquad
\frac{16}{9}\;\frac98=2.
$$

The intervening whole tone completes the span; it is not a defect preventing completion. These are the proportions generated by the Second Spanda's cross-reading. The composition gives each interval its place in a larger consonance without making the intervals identical.[^s3-music]

Another return makes a different demand. Twelve pure fifths do not equal seven octaves:

$$
\frac{(3/2)^{12}}{2^7}=\frac{531441}{524288}\ne1.
$$

That residual is the Pythagorean comma, not the whole tone `9/8`. Twelve-tone equal temperament distributes adjustment through the octave by using steps of `2^{1/12}`. Its twelve steps close exactly, while its fifth approximates rather than equals `3/2`. An instrument can therefore achieve a working cyclic closure by changing the intervals it preserves. The question is which relationship the tuning serves and what adjustment it makes audible, rather than whether closure is possible at all.[^s3-tuning]

Pitch class and pitch height distinguish return from ascent in another way. Map a positive frequency f to `log₂(f/f₀) mod 1`. Octave-related frequencies occupy the same point on the pitch-class circle, while a lift to the real logarithmic coordinate retains their register difference. One pitch-class phase gives a circle. A toroidal model requires two independently specified periodic coordinates; it cannot be obtained merely by calling octave recurrence circular twice.

Sound also needs a body whose conditions matter. For an ideal string fixed at both ends, a standing mode has the form `y(x,t)=A sin(nπx/L)cos(ωt)`, with `ω=nπv/L`. Length, wave speed and boundary conditions determine the admitted modes. Altering the support or moving from a string to a plate changes the problem and its pattern. This is why cymatic figures can disclose a powerful relation between excitation and form without becoming a universal stencil of QL. Their force as examples comes from the specific medium answering to a specific disturbance.[^s3-waves]

The original musical development also permits the player to stop. An accordion's alternating airflow can sustain a phrase through changing direction; the phrase can nevertheless reach its end. Breathing, recurrence and instrumental construction support the performance without sentencing it to perpetual continuation. In the later correction, fulfilment includes a genuine telos and the silence after it. A remainder may invite another movement, but it does not invalidate an achieved one. The completed relation becomes available for return, inheritance or release.

This gives the earlier limit a positive form. A determinate act can finish without claiming that every condition of its possibility has finished with it. Its result may retain an interval, a winding, an adjustment or a changed capacity in its receiver. The work of an account is to preserve the difference that matters to that act, not to accumulate every conceivable trace. What returns can then be recognised as a completed achievement within a world still capable of being encountered.

<a id="M30"></a>
<a id="s3-m30"></a>
### M30 — The Arche-Topos

A jigsaw begins with a useful promise. The picture on the lid gives the pieces a common destination: this patch belongs to that sky, this edge completes that building. Turning a piece, trying a fit and rejecting a false join make increasingly exact sense under the promised whole. The finished picture is an achievement. Without that initial orientation, the later discovery would have little to disturb.[^s3-jigsaw]

Now the picture's maker enters the world it depicts. A road continues beyond the edge; the building looks different from the other side; a feature hidden by one viewpoint appears from another. At first the answer seems to be more pieces. But pieces added under the old criterion keep extending the same projection. What is missing is not simply another patch of scenery. It is an account of how the picture was made: from where, over what domain, with which omissions, and through which rules another view can meet it.

The pieces begin to change office. They become local charts, each exact over an admitted domain, rather than fragments guaranteed to complete one final view. Their joins must now say how one passes into another. A road's continuation, a change of scale and an occluded face make different demands upon that passage. An honest join may preserve a disagreement or a gap where the translation has not been earned. The lid remains useful as one projection within the atlas. Its local success no longer gives it authority to decide in advance what the traveller can encounter.

Returning to the building does not undo the journey. The original façade is still recognisable, but it now belongs with the route around it and the previously unseen side. The torus supplied an exact formal witness to one aspect of such return: the surface-address can recur while the lifted path retains a displacement. The journey in the image carries more—revised expectation, another person's account, perhaps a reason to choose a different route. Its whole action reveals how a criterion is preserved by having its authority relocated. The mathematical example does not exhaust that action; it makes one of its relations sharply legible.

Arche-Topos names the differential field of this placing. It is not a concealed location at which all perspectives would finally coincide, since such a location would already be another position. It is the relating through which centre, circumstance, observer, object, path and horizon become mutually locatable. A determination reorganises what surrounds it; the surrounding field conditions what can be determined next. QL has followed this operation from the first distinction, through its self-relations and inverse phase, into contextual holding and return. The field is generated in the argument by those operations, not inferred from a resemblance among triangles, circles and doughnuts.[^s3-field]

The jigsaw's altered joins give the earlier distinction between a description and a transformation a precise test. Translating a trajectory into another chart preserves the motion being described. Changing the conditions which govern that motion can change the trajectory, its attractor or the basins from which an organisation is approached. Chart compatibility supplies none of those changes on its own. In a symbolic encounter, the corresponding question is whether the person has acquired another description of the same expectation or a changed capacity to receive and act. The atlas makes the descriptions comparable; the encounter must establish what has changed in the life.

Taylor's encounter with Van Eenwyk turns on this active relation. The notes follow perception beyond an incoming stimulus into past experience and expectation, then follow the symbol from familiar consciousness into an unknown implication and back. The resulting *Symbolon Dynamics* distinguishes the ordering capacity, the particular manifestation and the response that alters their next encounter. Amplification can move among images as among local disclosures; the symbol's effect on the person changes what will be available to disclose. The native `X/x` therefore enters psychology as a prior relation with a new burden: to show how recurrent form and a singular life belong together without treating the life as a replaceable example.[^s3-dynamics]

The psychoid relation follows from the place this differentiation occupies. Before psyche and matter can be compared, they must become distinguishable within one field of appearing and relation. That field is prior to their division in the order of dependence, not an earlier event on a physical clock. Subject conditions appearing; objective internality gives its constituted means; objects become determinate within their relation. The private ego is itself such a determination and cannot take the source-position. The Arche-Topos articulates this already-argued dependence as the field through which psychic and material positions become possible together.

Mathematics gives the relation an unusually public body. A construction can be repeated by another person, a failed inference can be identified, and an invariant can survive a change of description. Its form is therefore not exhausted by a private association. Yet the construction, its object and its correction remain moments of knowing, rather than an object supplying the entire condition of its own appearance. The psychoid claim keeps these two facts in one account: psychic and material determinations have a common originating relation, while their particular manifestations require different investigations. The Subject argument bears the ontological claim; the mathematical constructions articulate operations within it. A measured causal mechanism linking a particular psychic event and a particular physical event would be a further result, not something already furnished by this priority.[^s3-dependence]

The refractive image keeps the source relation visible. Light arrives through differently composed panes, held apart and together by their joins, and gives a changing projection within a room. The native appointments are specific: Bimba names the Original; QL names the ordered spectrum immanent to the light; MEF names the refractive operation of media, angles and joins; pratibimba names the situated reflection. Changing the sun's angle, the pane or the viewer changes the image. Following those changes back through their conditions distinguishes a reflection from a picture that claims to have produced its own light. This is the image's argument, not an identification of consciousness with electromagnetic radiation.[^s3-refraction]

For an instrument, the consequence is practical. Its output should remain related to the sources, selections and transformations that made it possible. Another participant needs to know what can be retraced, what can be recomputed and where an interpretation rather than a reversible map has crossed the seam. Some results should be retained; some should be corrected; some inquiries should be released. A system that merely keeps producing answers has not thereby performed return. It needs a way for the achieved determination to alter, or cease to command, the next act. Whether a particular implementation provides that capacity is an operational question, not an accomplishment conferred by the vocabulary.

The native shorthand now carries two related but distinct readings. The defining circuit returns to the relation it articulated:

$$
0/1\;\longrightarrow\;4+2\;\longrightarrow\;(5\!\to\!0)\;\longrightarrow\;0/1.
$$

The processual traversal also unfolds the returned relation from its other phase:

$$
0/1\to4+2\to(5\to0)\to1/0\to4'+2'\to(5'\to0')\to0/1.
$$

The prime marks the conjugate passage, not an extra pair of substances. Each parent contains a whole body; the inverse reading changes the offices its contents occupy. An achieved return can become the condition of a further inquiry, while the actual inquiry that achieved it is allowed to be complete. This is why recognition cannot be replaced by a requirement that everything run again.

In the original note “Maths and the Mystery are One,” exact definition and questionability belong to one task. The mystery is what calls for an account and what keeps the account's conditions from disappearing behind its result. The mathematics has given that thought positive substance: an invariant together with its transformation, a chart together with its domain, a quotient together with its lift, a musical completion together with the relation it preserves. None becomes less exact by admitting how it is situated.[^s3-mystery]

The traveller can put the pieces down. The picture remains useful, and the journey remains more than the picture can contain. On returning to a familiar place, a formerly hidden face may now be expected; a trusted route may be reconsidered. The acquired form participates in a changed encounter. What happens when that change concerns the person who recognises the form—when a dream, an image or another's answer alters what the person can bear, desire or do?

*[Section room](section-rooms/05-psychoid-flowering/ROOM.md)*

## §4 — Psychoid Flowering

<a id="M31"></a>
<!-- M31 / §4 #0 -->
### Number and meaning

An ordering relation can change the person for whom its terms belong together. A mathematical construction makes a transformation available to thought; a dream, an encounter or a work of art can make an established understanding of oneself impossible to inhabit in the old way. In the first case we ask what follows from the construction. In the second we must also ask what happens to the one who follows it. The differential field developed in the preceding section reaches its psychic life here: a distinction acquires significance, gathers feeling, governs conduct and sometimes changes the conditions under which further distinctions can be made.

The psychoid relation established through the Arche-Topos now has to be encountered from within a life. Number can be grasped inwardly without the objects it subsequently orders; those objects can also resist an interpretation of what the relation means. Exactness constrains the thinking that apprehends it, while apprehension gives the exact relation a place in an inquiry. Psychic and physical determinations retain their different warrants within the common ordering field. What follows concerns how that field becomes significant to the person participating in it.[^s4-01]

Carl Gustav Jung and Wolfgang Pauli approach this problem through a disagreement that changes their proposed common ground. In the correspondence, a common ground does not emerge because psychology acquires the prestige of physics or physics acquires an evocative vocabulary. Pauli presses Jung over what an account of non-causal order must explain. A meaningful event need not coincide in clock time with the dream to which it is related; conversely, unpredictability does not make an event free of order. Their discussions of temporal separation, prediction and probability require distinctions within the very phenomena that the word *synchronicity* might seem to gather. The meaningful connection and the causal histories of its terms have to be stated separately. Otherwise the proposed connection borrows its apparent force from an equivocation.[^s4-02]

The pressure becomes sharper in their 1953 exchange. Pauli distinguishes the concepts by which order can be expressed from the occurrence that can be ascertained here and now. Mathematics cannot simply be placed inside psychology as a collection of mental productions: its relations constrain the thinking that apprehends them. Yet a physical account that treats the conditions of apprehension as irrelevant has excluded part of the problem it claims to describe. His proposed common ground requires concepts which can hold both sides. Jung, in turn, develops the psychoid beyond the ordinary meaning of the psychic. The fact that the psyche is the medium through which we know does not make every object a private psychic fabrication.

Pauli's comparison includes three languages: physical, theological-metaphysical and psychological. Each can articulate an ordering relation which the others do not exhaust. His reading of the three rings places unity in human relation and an empty centre, rather than in the victory of one vocabulary. The common ground is approached through their differentiated participation. Mathematical objects and the psychic experience of mathematics can remain distinct while their relation becomes a legitimate question. Jung's reply likewise preserves a difference: professional physical language is not, by itself, a sufficient interpretation of what a dream has brought into a life.

The disagreement persists when Pauli proposes an enlarged physics capable of adopting psychology. He insists that the adopting discipline would undergo the greater transformation: what physics took itself to be would have to change. Jung still resists adoption. A discipline's willingness to expand does not establish that its new language can receive the other's object without remainder. Their correspondence has reached a problem within the proposed act of unification itself. How can the common account be made without its maker already deciding which participant will supply the whole?

Jung's return to natural number gives the shared inquiry a definite object. Number has an inward formal aspect and an outward quantitative application, while its elementary configurations also acquire symbolic force. A quantitative result cannot establish a symbolic interpretation on its own, and a compelling symbol does not measure a physical effect. But the separation of those warrants leaves their common ordering relation to be understood. Pauli's later resistance to loosely specified hyperspace preserves the same demand: dimensions and transformations must have articulated meanings before their names can connect different fields. The correspondence advances through these corrections, with each participant's resistance changing the question the other has to answer.[^s4-03]

This gives ordinary and extraordinary experience an exact place. An experience can alter attention, valuation, memory and action before agreement has been reached about its cause. A dream, a coincidence felt as significant, a contemplative disclosure or an encounter described as supernatural can enter inquiry with its full weight as a psychic fact. Receiving that fact means attending to what occurred, how it was articulated and what it changed. Physical explanation, historical interpretation and metaphysical judgment remain further acts of inquiry. They need not be settled in advance for the experience to matter, and they must not be silently settled by the vocabulary in which it was first reported. Jung's treatment of religious images makes this distinction productive: their psychic reality has consequences that neither a declaration of external existence nor a dismissal as error can exhaust.[^s4-04]

<!-- s4-pauli-whole -->
Pauli's egg dream gives this relation a body. An unnamed woman brings a bird, and the bird lays a large egg. The egg divides of itself into two complete eggs. Pauli has so far only watched. When he approaches, he discovers a third, blue egg already in his hand. He now divides this egg himself, and two whole blue eggs result. The first division happened before him; the second includes his action. Both preserve the egg's wholeness rather than producing broken halves. The blue egg was already in his hand when he discovered it: participation precedes his recognition that he is participating.

The four eggs then appear as two identical rows of trigonometric expressions, each containing the cosine and sine of half an angle. They become a quotient of complex conjugates:

$$
\frac{\cos(\delta/2)+i\sin(\delta/2)}
     {\cos(\delta/2)-i\sin(\delta/2)}
= e^{i\delta}.
$$

Pauli recognises the circle and speaks for the first time in the sequence. The formula disappears; the circle itself appears. The seven-picture course has passed from a woman with her bird, through spontaneous division, the blue egg discovered in his hand and performed division, into trigonometric and complex articulation, speech and the circle. Its moments belong to one movement. Remove the change from spectator to participant and the dream becomes an assortment of number symbols. Remove the numerical transformation and its passage into recognition loses the exact relation through which it proceeds.[^s4-05]

The equation permits a precise check. For real `δ`, the denominator has modulus one and never vanishes. The numerator and denominator are `e^{iδ/2}` and `e^{−iδ/2}`; their quotient is `e^{iδ}`. A fixed value of `δ` gives a point, and variation through a full turn traces the unit circle. The mathematical relation is independent of whether a dreamer finds it moving. Its symbolic force, however, depends upon the event in which it comes to be recognised. Pauli arrives at the circle through a distinction that first acts without his intervention and then becomes his own act.

The two rows have the same mathematical form, but their eggs do not have the same narrative history. One pair came about before the observer; another came about through him. Exact equivalence can retain a relation while leaving out how its terms were achieved. The dream restores that difference by carrying the observer into the operation. When the circle appears, the result is no longer only an object whose regularity he witnesses. It is an order he has helped articulate and can now recognise as one. The final speech is part of that arrival: the recogniser can say what has happened only after his position within it has changed.

This is stronger than noticing that four eggs resemble a quaternity. The whole narrative discloses how an apparently external order can become a relation in which the recogniser finds himself implicated. Its truth-bearing work is to make that change in participation encounterable; the algebra makes one relation within it independently checkable. A theorem can correct a mistaken account of the circle. The dream can correct an account of the theorem's reception which has omitted the person undergoing it. Neither correction is supplied by the other alone.

<!-- s4-calculation-care -->
My own encounter with the correspondence begins at this crossing. If number can conduct both exact relation and symbolic transformation, mathematical mediation need not be confined to calculation whose consequences for the calculator disappear from the account. Its qualitative life concerns what a pattern enables a person to receive, distinguish and become. Meaning is present wherever an articulation changes the world from which further articulation proceeds.[^s4-06]

Calculation then has two related responsibilities. Its subject matter can resist a preferred result: the quantities, assumptions and operations must bear examination. Its recipient can also be changed by the manner in which the result is made available. A calculation may help someone recognise an alternative, or make a local measure seem like a final account of what matters. Both results can arise from arithmetically correct work. Care for the subject matter and care for the receiving person therefore belong to the conduct of the mediation. They require an answer that can be corrected, and a recipient able to question the criterion under which it was produced.

The technological possibility begins here. An instrument can make the form of a person's mediation available to them: which question was asked, what was selected, what was left aside and why the resulting answer acquired weight. The encounter can change how the instrument is made and used. Its achievement would then include a changed power of reception, rather than only an additional object to receive. To understand that difference we have to follow the force by which a form holds attention in the first place.

The eight determinations of the primordial Symbolon keep this movement articulate. From the bare relational capacity, `−/−`, a form becomes available as `0/1`; its appearance both questions and asserts, `?/!`; withdrawal and extension give the encounter force, `−/+`; a recurrent capacity becomes recognisable through its particular instance, `X/x`; lived presence and sayable determination meet as `AM/IS`; an inexhaustible horizon enters an exact local change, `∞/dx`; and the achieved form turns back toward its ground, `1/0`. These are the native determinations already derived, now received in psychic life. The dream, theorem and interpretation each traverse a relation whose ground remains active in what it makes determinate. Within a life, that activity takes formed and affective powers which can support the person or claim to speak for the whole.

<a id="M32"></a>
<!-- M32 / §4 #1 -->
### A person within the pattern

The accusation has remained unsent, but the waiting person still reaches for the screen. Knowing how the rejection story formed has not removed the pull of it. An ambiguous sentence from the earlier exchange acquires its hard edge again; memories of other silences are readily available. A defensive message could provoke the withdrawal it anticipates. Silence could become another test which the other is expected to understand without being told.

The account examined in §2 can therefore survive its own explanation. Its criterion is now visible, yet it still offers a familiar way to bear the delay and a course to take. The other may actually be withdrawing. The further question concerns the investment through which this one possibility commands attention before an answer arrives, and the change that would let a real answer determine what follows.[^s4-07]

The image, the complex and the archetype have different offices. The image is this appearance: a silent screen, a remembered face, a sentence heard in a particular tone. The complex gathers such appearances into an affective organisation of memory, expectation, bodily response and action. Archetypal dynamics concern the formative possibilities that can recur across different images and acquired organisations. One image does not contain its complex, and one complex does not exhaust the power of formation which its history has given a local shape. A living symbol can change their relation. It makes an appearance disclose something that the established criterion had prevented the person from encountering.

The native `X/x` distinguishes determining capacity from the indefinite particular through which it becomes manifest. The lower-case term is indefinite because an inventory of its properties cannot finish everything it may become or disclose; it is particular because this encounter has a history and consequences which another cannot simply replace. Its psychic refraction lets an archetypal power become legible through an image without being confined to that image. A person can recognise a recurrent organisation without treating recurrence as destiny. The capacity exceeds its present settlement.

The same distinction keeps ego and Self from becoming rival names for one executive centre. The ego supplies an orientation from which commitments can be made and responsibility undertaken. Complexes can interrupt, support or redirect it; collective images and bodily conditions sustain possibilities it did not author. The Self names the whole-forming relation in which these different agencies belong. If it were only a larger ego, individuation would culminate in the conquest of every local agency by a more powerful ruler. Jung's warning about ego–Self inflation requires a different change: the relation to totality must become more adequate without awarding totality to the conscious position that recognises it.[^s4-08]

<!-- s4-energetic-investment -->
The rejection story still offers protection even when its reasoning is exposed. It ends the open waiting, gives the hurt a cause and preserves a practised identity: the one who sees disappointment coming, the one who will not be made a fool of again. The person may understand this service and continue to need it. Relinquishing the story now means meeting the desire and uncertainty it had organised, without yet knowing whether another response will be bearable.

Libido names the psychic investment through which this difference matters. It concerns the disposition of attention, desire, fear and value: what draws a person toward something, what makes them recoil, what they will expend themselves defending. A description of the pattern can show how one thought recruits another. An energetic account asks why these thoughts have acquired the power to hold a life. The remembered face may remain recognisable and the old history still be known, while the investment in their verdict changes. The person may no longer have to organise the next encounter around defending it. Conversely, a newly acquired explanation may coexist with the old investment. The distinction between pattern and charge is needed to tell these cases apart.[^s4-09]

A favourable replacement story may leave that investment untouched. Perhaps the other is simply busy. Perhaps they are composing a considerate reply. Either is possible, but adopting the more comforting hypothesis can preserve the same demand: I must know in advance that I am safe. The person remains occupied with obtaining a guarantee from an image. What has changed is its sign, not the dependence upon it. The next delay can reactivate the same jurisdiction.

A more consequential change begins when the protective function becomes perceptible. The person notices not only the thought of rejection but the relief supplied by having settled what the silence means. The story is no longer simply the world announcing itself; it is also an act through which the person has tried to make the world bearable. Its history may deserve considerable care. Sensitivity to withdrawal may have been learned where attention to small signs was useful. Recognising that history does not require the sensitivity to disappear. It changes the claim that every present relation must be governed by the conditions under which that sensitivity first became necessary.

The uncertainty now has to be lived. No completed interpretation stands in for the other's answer. The person can ask a question whose answer is not secretly prescribed, wait without making the waiting a punishment, or acknowledge a wish without turning it into an accusation. These possibilities have a cost: they expose a desire which defensive certainty had protected. They also make another kind of knowledge possible. An answer may disappoint, reassure, complicate or refuse. Something other than the demand for confirmation can now determine what happens next.

The change is therefore not measured by whether the answer is pleasant. A refusal received as a refusal may be a more truthful encounter than an affectionate answer compulsively interrogated until it sounds like rejection. Care turns toward the reality of the relationship, including the other person's freedom within it. The original desire has not been extinguished. It has become capable of sharing the field with a desire whose course it does not control. Power previously spent on maintaining certainty can enter the more exact work of responding.

This distinction keeps the other person from becoming merely the vehicle of an internal transformation. An other-self discovered in a projection can disclose something about the one who projects. The actual other can answer from a life which that discovery does not contain. In the native relation, the Other belongs within the shared Mono, not within my private person. Recognition of a common ground consequently increases the need to hear this particular response. It removes the warrant for treating another centre as a missing piece of my self-description.[^s4-10]

Van Eenwyk helps to distinguish this passage from restoration of a familiar equilibrium. A recurring organisation can receive many experiences within its range. A symbolic encounter can also expose the boundary of that organisation and make another way of receiving experience possible. The second movement changes the interpreter, not just the interpretation. Its unfamiliarity is part of its difficulty: the knowledge that will become possible cannot all be possessed before the passage is made. Enough continuity must remain for the person to bear the change. Mere destabilisation is no proof of growth; reinstating a closure already shown to be inadequate is no sufficient account of recovery.[^s4-11]

The attractor comparison states one aspect of the difference. Different trajectories can settle into a recognisable organisation, while a change in conditions can make another organisation possible. Its psychological use distinguishes a further occurrence within a regime from a transformation of the regime. A literal model of a particular psyche would additionally require specified variables, evolution and observations. The lived distinction gives that modelling a question to answer: did the encounter merely produce another response which the existing organisation could accommodate, or did it change what the person can receive and do?

In its psychic articulation, `X = x` gives the Self's office to the relating sign. The individual is the particular through which the whole becomes a question and a possible recognition. The equals sign does not abolish the distinction between archetypal capacity and its instance. It makes their belonging together the work of the equation. To solve only for the ego as an isolated object would omit the relation which makes it intelligible; to substitute an undifferentiated whole for the person would omit the life in which the recognition must occur. The native equation keeps both terms and changes the manner of their identification.[^s4-12]

The return `x → X → x` follows that change into conduct. A particular formation becomes transparent to a determining capacity it had expressed without containing. Recognition returns into this person, with this history, asking this question differently. The second `x` has a body, commitments and consequences still to meet. Likewise, `IS → AM` returns an account to the identifying activity of the one who gives it. A description of rejection becomes consequential when its speaker can recognise their own participation in its repetition. The description has reached the act by which description is being made.

Knowledge can be accurately repeated by someone whose criterion remains untouched. The existential resolution developed in my earlier inquiry concerns the knower's dependence upon the forms through which they know. A conception can give orientation and security; its dissolution releases significance from the particular end at which it had been arrested. Inquiry has motive because what is settled can reopen and what is reopened can acquire a more adequate form. Permanent tension is no more its goal than premature agreement. A tension has done its work when a real resolution becomes possible without sacrificing the differences that made it necessary.[^s4-13]

The energetic account extends through the body. In the vocabulary of prāṇa, life is articulated as circulation: inhaling and exhaling, drawing in and giving out, currents differentiated within a living activity. A frightened interpretation may accompany a narrowed breath, tightened attention and readiness to act. Words, feeling and bodily preparation belong to the same lived situation without becoming identical descriptions of it. Attending to the rhythm approaches the situation through another of its actual conditions. A pause in the rush toward an answer can become a place in which the demand behind the answer is felt. The pause matters because the next act need not simply continue the force of the previous one.

The Śāktic account asks a further question: what is the activity by which a world becomes manifest in these determinate forms? Śakti names manifestation-power, including disclosure, maintenance, concealment and recognition. In the contracted situation an interpretation is illuminated so completely that the act of illumination disappears from view. A world of signs seems simply given. Recognition turns toward the making-visible itself. The field disclosed through fear is recognised as a field disclosed through fear; this reveals both the fear's reality and its limitation. Appearance continues, but its present organisation no longer stands alone as its own source.

Spanda gives withdrawal and extension their place within that activity. A manifestation comes forth; its formed limit does not exhaust the capacity from which it comes. Withdrawal retains a reserve from which another determination can arise. The native `−/+` holds these directions together. Where every withdrawal is experienced as extinction, a formed position must cling to itself at any cost. When withdrawal preserves the capacity to appear otherwise, relinquishment can make another act possible. What the achieved act could not use up becomes the condition of its transformation.

Libido, prāṇa, Śakti and Spanda thus enter at different necessities in the argument. Investment explains the disposition of value and attention; circulation gives the body's differentiated traffic; manifestation-power concerns the disclosure and concealment of a determinate world; pulsation relates the formed issue to its reserve. In mantra, a formed sound can organise breath, gather attention and become the occasion for recognising its own appearing. Cadence, psychic investment and recognitive activity cooperate here through the different changes each makes possible.[^s4-14]

<!-- s4-plasmic-reciprocity -->
The later plasmic development brings the relation between a whole and its local determinations into a material field. Its starting question is how a multiplicity can help constitute the order through which its own members move. In a self-consistent plasma account, the distribution of charged particles supplies charge and current to the field equations. The electromagnetic fields in turn condition the motion described by that distribution. A proposed field cannot simply be accepted regardless of the particles that source it, nor can their motion be specified while disregarding the field to which they contribute.

Cordonnier and his collaborators make this closure explicit for stationary, cylindrically symmetric, magnetically confined plasmas. They obtain an equilibrium distribution under stated constraints, calculate its source terms and solve the resulting coupled field problem. The calculation has to return through what it used as its starting distribution. Its self-consistency requires the particle distribution and field to satisfy the coupled equations under the same assumptions.[^s4-15]

The native `(0/1)/(1/0)` reads the two directions together. One orientation follows the field into its local expression; the other follows the local contribution into the field it helps determine. Neither is discarded once the other is recognised. Mono names the whole in its continuous and inexhaustible office; Poly names its differentiated multiplicity. The whole is legible through its differentiated expressions, and each expression through the continuous relation which makes it possible. A local determination belongs to a wider order, while that order is actively disclosed through determinations rather than remaining an inert background.

The `4+2` keeps both orientations available. As derived earlier, the terms of the inverse parents yield four explicit relations, while the two whole-bearing poles are retained. A formed account can follow those relations without consuming the whole into its selected products. In the material comparison this means keeping the return from distribution to field and from field to distribution, together with the conditions under which the account is posed. The sixfold articulates the relation through which the physical model is read; that model supplies its own variables and equations.

The associated `∞/Δx` distinguishes an inexhaustible horizon from an exact local measure. A finite determination acquires its meaning within a containing field, and a change of local conditions can alter what that field permits. The infinite office is not a very large unmeasured physical quantity. Nor is a boundary merely an impediment: a boundary condition makes a particular physical solution possible. The Śāktic reading gives measure a similarly productive office. Māyā articulates a finite world in which definite acts can occur. Contraction becomes binding when its measure claims to exhaust the activity it has made locally available. Recognition restores that measure to its work rather than dissolving the world it measures.

The toroidal construction supplies circulation and differentiated directions of return; plasma supplies a material question about collective fields and local motion. Their conjunction can be investigated without pretending that the topology alone solves the physical equations. The present cylindrical witness establishes a particular self-consistency, not the necessity that every plasma be a torus. The philosophical gain lies in the reciprocal conditioning which the calculation makes exact. It allows the whole–part relation to be followed as an operation rather than inferred from the resemblance of two circular pictures.

This returns the energetic argument to the person. A local image contributes to an organisation of attention through which subsequent images will be received. A response changes the relationship that will condition the next response. The physical distribution and the psychic image have different objects and warrants, but the organising relation is real in each account: what is produced participates in the conditions of further production. No conversion of psychic investment into electrical charge is needed to understand that relation. Its specificity is what allows one register to sharpen a question in another.[^s4-16]

The psyche also has to assimilate what it receives. In my reading of Neumann, this requirement passes through the body's elementary traffic: hunger, intake, digestion and issue. What enters can become a new capacity of the creature that takes it in. Receiving information is an earlier moment than becoming able to live from it. A person may collect increasingly subtle descriptions of their difficulty and still receive the next silence as before. An assimilated encounter changes the conditions of the next reception. Knowledge has become nourishment when it can sustain a different act.[^s4-17]

The devouring counterpart makes the limit clear. A system of interpretation can consume everything without allowing anything to change it. Each new voice becomes material for its existing certainty. Its hunger is maintained by the success with which it converts difference into the same. Assimilation permits what has been received to alter the receiver's capacities. It can culminate in enough: enough understanding to act, enough satisfaction for the present task to end, enough confidence to leave another person unpossessed. A living return includes release.

Watson's encounter with Levinas sharpens this change of value. The other can interrupt the measure by which satisfaction was being pursued. In the reply example, obtaining reassurance gives way to learning how this relation can actually be lived. The wish remains, but it no longer dictates the measure of everything that appears. The change is not merely a greater force winning on an unchanged scale of self-interest. The scale itself has become answerable. This is the energetic question at its ethical limit: what makes another's reality effective in an act which had been organised around securing one's own account?[^s4-18]

Individuation names this becoming more distinctly oneself through a wider relation. A history, a body, a capacity for judgment and the consequences of action are retained. Recognition resituates what they have achieved. It gives a local organisation its place within a life whose possibilities it does not exhaust. The whole is active as the capacity to bear and transform differentiated relations. That capacity has a more difficult test than reconciling two favourable interpretations: it must also bear an opposition whose contrary cannot be removed without falsifying the whole.

<a id="M33"></a>
<!-- M33 / §4 #2 -->
### Wholeness that can change

A quaternity gives a field differentiated breadth. Its four terms can prevent one opposition from exhausting the possible relations: the other side of an encounter need not be only the negation of the side presently occupied. Yet four names arranged around a centre do not by themselves establish wholeness. Their relation to what generates them, and to what their encounter changes, has to remain active. Otherwise a diagram of completeness becomes another image which experience must satisfy.

Jung's distinction between four functions and two attitudes makes the difference between a field and its orientation useful here. Thinking, feeling, sensation and intuition are functions in his typology; introversion and extraversion describe orientations through which functions operate. In the introduction to *Psychologische Typen*, Jung corrects an earlier tendency to identify thinking with introversion and feeling with extraversion. Both attitudes occur, with different predominance, and a function can take either direction. The correction preserves distinctions which the earlier classification could not accommodate.[^s4-19]

The native senarius reads four differentiated operations together with their implicate opening and return. That is the `4+2` already derived from a distinction's self-relation, not the discovery of six Jungian functions. Four functions oriented in two ways and four manifest positions with two implicate offices answer different questions.
